full_judgment: 2. The case, of the petitioner, in brief, is that the house bearing holding No. 26/B/A, 2nd Colony, Mirpur, Dhaka was allotted to Abdur Rahim by the Government vide registered lease deed in the year 1953 and the said lessee got possession of the disputed house, who died leaving behind one daughter namely Rabeya Khatun, who also died on 3-10-79 leaving behind her husband Md Osman Gani and three minor sons and one minor daughter; thereafter, Osman Gani transferred the disputed house to Abul Kalam Khan who was put into possession thereof. The purchaser Abul Kalam Khan got his name mutated in accordance with, law and the property has been recorded in RS khatian in the name of the purchaser Abul Karam Khan, who also got water connection as well as electricity connection and gas connection for the said property and has been paying all bills to the Government. In this way the petitioner acquired right, title and possession over the disputed house in question. The further case of the petitioner is that in order to fortify his right, title and possession over the case land he filed Title Suit No. 306 of 1983 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka for declaration of title in the disputed land against the Government on 13-6-83. The Government on receiving the summons appeared in the Court on 27-2-84 and prayed for time to file written statement but later on, the Government did not or could not take any step in the said suit. Ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte on 13-8-84. Against which the Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 229 of 1986 before the learned Munsif, 1st Court, Dhaka who upon hearing both the parties was pleased to dismiss the same by his judgment and order dated 7-9-89 (Annexure-H).
